Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Apex Asset Management Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question during the Q&A, press star then one on your telephone keypad. There will be an opportunity to ask a question after the presentation. Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Asset Management's Q3 2024 results. Joining me on today's call are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Investment Officer; David Kim, Head of Distribution; Elena Vasquez, Head of Operations; and Robert Kline, Head of Risk Management.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that some of the statements made today may be forward-looking. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. I'm pleased to report on our performance for Q3 2024. We achieved solid results this quarter, driven by resilient market tailwinds and strong organic growth from net inflows. Our AUM grew to $1.2 trillion.

Michael Chen: Thank you, Sarah. From a financial perspective, Apex Asset Management delivered strong results in Q3 2024. Our revenue was $1.2 billion, representing a 9% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by a combination of robust AUM expansion and favorable product mix shifts. Our expenses were $850 million, resulting in net income of $280 million. Our expense ratio improved due to scale efficiencies and targeted cost management.

Before diving deeper into the numbers, let me provide some color on our assets under management, which ended the quarter at $1.2 trillion, up 8% quarter-over-quarter and 12% year-over-year. This marks our 11th consecutive quarter of AUM growth, propelled by a favorable mix of market performance contributing about $85 billion, or 65% of the total increase, and resilient net inflows of $42 billion. Global equities led the way, with our long-only equity strategies capturing strong gains from a 9.2% rally in the S&P 500 and 7.8% in the MSCI World Index. Our U.S. large-cap active funds added $32 billion through appreciation, while fixed income contributed a net $12 billion despite some early-quarter duration pressures that we mitigated actively. Alternatives, now 22% of AUM at around $265 billion, added $18 billion from private credit and infrastructure realizations.

Net flows were strong across channels, with institutional inflows of $28 billion led by sustainable multi-asset mandates and retail/wealth at $14 billion, highlighted by $22 billion into ETFs like our ESG Core suite. Regionally, North America drove 55%, EMEA 30%, and APAC the rest, reflecting our diversified footprint. Passive strategies now at 38% of AUM underscore the industry shift, but our active equities remain a key profit driver.

Turning to fund performance, which continues to underscore the strength of our active management edge amid inflation pressures, Fed tightening, and geopolitical headwinds like Russia-Ukraine and U.S.-China tensions. Across our platform, our strategies outpaced benchmarks and peer medians in 78% of rated funds per Morningstar Q3 data. In U.S. equities, our Large-Cap Growth Fund at $28 billion AUM returned 22.4% YTD, beating the S&P 500's 19.8% by 260 bps and peers at 18.2%, with three-year alpha of 140 bps from tech picks like NVIDIA and Microsoft. Small-cap value at $15 billion posted 14.7% YTD versus Russell 2000 Value's 11.3%, aided by quality screens and quant models.

Internationally, our $42 billion International Equity Fund delivered 16.8% YTD, ahead of MSCI EAFE by 160 bps, with wins in European renewables and Asia consumer plays. EM Alpha at $18 billion shone at 12.6% YTD versus 8.9% benchmark. In fixed income, Core Bond at $65 billion yielded 2.1% YTD against a -1.2% aggregate drawdown, via duration shortening and IG corporates. High-yield at $22 billion crushed at 8.4%, and alts like our Global Macro Hedge at $35 billion returned 9.8% net, top-decile versus HFRX.

Now, on efficiency ratios, particularly our expense ratio at a firm-wide 42 bps for Q3, down 16 bps YoY and our lowest in five years. This positions us competitively, with ETFs at 14 bps, active at 68 bps, and alts/SMAs at 91 bps. Driven by AUM scale to $728 billion peak, automation via our GAP Efficiency Engine reducing middle-office costs 22%, AI fee optimization, cloud migration, and outsourcing. Trends show steady decline from 65 bps in 2021, varying regionally—39 bps North America, 52 bps EMEA, 61 bps APAC—with targets sub-38 bps by year-end.

Operating expenses totaled $312 million in the quarter, up 4% YoY but flat sequentially, at 42% of revenue. Breakdown: compensation and benefits $168 million (54%, up 6% on incentives), technology/data $52 million (17%, up 12% for AI pilots), distribution/marketing $38 million (12%, up 2%), G&A $28 million (9%, down 3%), and amortization/other $26 million (8%). This supports 38% operating margins.

On trends in operating margin, we hit 36.2% in Q3, up 410 bps YoY to a TTM 35.8%, ahead of peers like BlackRock's 34.5%. Multi-year expansion from 28.4% in FY22, fueled by 14% revenue growth to $2.8 billion, performance fees, and expense leverage, with mix shifts to high-margin alts.

For guidance, Q4 revenue $1.25-$1.3 billion (4-8% sequential growth) on $540-550 billion average AUM, $15-20 billion flows, and 2-4% markets. FY2025 revenue $5.1-5.3 billion (6-10% growth). Q4 opex $850-875 million (32-33% margin), FY2025 $3.5-3.6 billion. Confident in mid-single-digit growth and FCF for buybacks/dividends.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, Michael. On the investment front, we continue to focus on delivering strong risk-adjusted returns for our clients. Our key strategies performed well, particularly in equities and alternatives. We are navigating the current market environment by emphasizing quality tilts, duration management, and volatility targeting. We launched our ESG Optimizer tool-enhanced products this quarter, and the early reception has been positive, with $22 billion in net inflows into sustainable strategies.

David Kim: Thank you, Lisa. From a distribution perspective, we saw strong inflows into our ETF funds. Our efforts to expand our reach in APAC are paying off, as evidenced by 42% surge in digital AUM from Singapore and Hong Kong, plus robust ETF growth capturing thematic flows.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you, David. Operationally, we've made significant progress in improving our technology infrastructure. This has resulted in increased efficiency and reduced operational risk. We've allocated $285 million in fiscal 2023, up 22% YoY, to our Digital Wealth Ecosystem, migrating 85% of systems to AWS/Azure hybrid cloud for 35% TCO cut and 4x speeds via GAP Horizon. AI/data investments with Snowflake/Palantir add 150 bps alpha in quants, ESG Optimizer at 72% adoption. Client tools like GAP AutoPilot boost retention 25%, advisor portals lower minimums. ROI includes $92 million savings, NPS to 82, with pilots in blockchain tokenization for $50 billion illiquids. Positions us for 15% digital growth.

Robert Kline: Thank you, Elena. From a risk management perspective, we continue to maintain a robust framework to identify, assess, and mitigate risks across the organization. We have enhanced our monitoring of market volatility and credit spreads, and are taking steps to address potential vulnerabilities. This includes our proprietary volatility targeting capping tracking error at 4%, NLP sentiment analysis, and AI-driven VaR tools cutting computation 80%, alongside post-LDI learnings for pensions.

Sarah Thompson: In summary, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering value to our shareholders. We are focused on executing our strategic priorities and capitalizing on the opportunities ahead. This includes targeting 10-12% AUM growth, accelerating ETF launches, and leveraging tech for efficiency and alpha.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. To ask a question, press star then one. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more details on the drivers behind your AUM growth this quarter?

Sarah Thompson: Thanks, John. As Michael outlined, our $1.2 trillion AUM reflects $85 billion from markets—equities capturing 112% of S&P upside, fixed income resilient via convexity—and $42 billion organic flows, institutional alts leading at $28 billion, retail ETFs at $22 billion net. YTD flows $128 billion position us strongly.

John Smith: Thank you. And a follow-up on your revenue guidance assumptions?

Michael Chen: Sure, John. Q4 revenue $1.25-1.3 billion assumes $15-20 billion flows led by $10 billion ETFs like APEXSPX, $5 billion alts, 2-4% markets, fees at 42 bps offset by $150 million performance fees. FY25 $5.1-5.3 billion on $580-600 billion AUM, mix to 55% equities/multi-asset.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morningstar.

Emily Chen: Good morning. Could you elaborate on the performance of your U.S. Large-Cap Growth Fund?

Lisa Patel: Happy to, Emily. The fund returned 22.4% YTD, +260 bps over S&P 500 and +420 bps peers, three-year 11.2% annualized with 0.92 Sharpe. NVIDIA and Microsoft drove 45% attribution, underweight cyclicals smartly positioned us.

Emily Chen: And how is the new ESG Optimizer product performing relative to expectations?

David Kim: Exceeding, Emily. 72% institutional adoption, $22 billion inflows to ESG overlays amid net-zero push. Complements our ETF suite, driving 20% retail flows via ApexOne platform.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan.

David Lee: Can you provide more color on the operational efficiencies you've gained?

Elena Vasquez: Absolutely, David. Tech investments yielded 15x ROI on $150 million spend: NAV automation cut hours 65%, AI fee tiers save $12 million annually, AWS phase 2 $9 million G&A cut. Digital CAC down 40% to $450, 92% straight-through processing.

Operator: Our next question comes from Rachel Gomez with Barclays.

Rachel Gomez: What are your thoughts on the current regulatory environment and its impact on your risk profile?

Robert Kline: Good question, Rachel. Robust monitoring of regs like SEC T+1, EU AI Act, SFDR via RegTech automating 95% reporting, slashing costs 28%. Volatility models cap TE at 4%, gen-AI VaR 80% faster, buffers like $50 billion privates dry powder mitigate inflation/recession risks.

Operator: Thank you. There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Sarah Thompson for closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Apex Asset Management. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
